newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY APV TO SELL STAKE IN AGRANA UNIT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY APV TO SELL STAKE IN AGRANA UNIT.

text.p: The Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt's board has decided to sell APV's minority stake in the sugar factory Petohazi Cukoripari Rt to a firm owned by Petohazi's management and sugar beet growers, APV said in a press release on Wednesday.

The firm, called Betacukor Befektetesi Kft, will be able to aquire the 25.77 percent stake mainly in exchange for compensation coupons , the statement said, without indicating how many coupons it would have to pay.
Austria's Agrana owns the rest of Petohazi's shares.
APV said that the deal would allow suppliers and staff to have a blocking minority of 25 percent plus one shares in Petohazi.
It added that APV would like to sell similar stakes to the staff and suppliers of Hungary's other 11 sugar factories wherever possible.
Agrana, which is itself controlled by Austria's Raiffeisen and Germany's Sudzucker , has a majority stake seven Hungarian sugar factories.
Eridania Beghin-Say controls four factories and Eastern Sugar, a joint venture between Britain's Tate & Lyle and France's Saint-Louis , has a majority of the shares in one factory.
Since 1992, the Hungarian government has been issuing compensation coupons to victims of expropriations and persecution by the country's former communist and fascist governments, and their heirs.
The coupons have a lively secondary market.
Beet suppliers -- mainly communist-era cooperatives -- received the coupons when they gave out tracts of their land in exchange for the coupons during farm privatisations earlier this decade.
